Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
Despite service of notice, no one appeared on behalf of the complainant.
2. The applicant seeks enlargement on bail in FIR No.137 of 2023, under Section 376-D IPC and Section 5/6 of POCSO Act, Police Station Tadiyawan, District Hardoi.
3. In terms of the FIR, it was alleged that the daughter of the informant aged about 15 years was sleeping at home and subsequently, she was found missing.

During search, she came to know that the co-accused Golu Shukla enticed her daughter with the help of the applicant and other co-accused Alok Kumar Awasthi vs The State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home, ... on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172872941/
1 persons.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the statement under Section 161 of Cr.P.C., the victim stated that Golu Shukla had formed physical relation with the victim.
The allegation of physical relation against the applicant was also made in the statement under Section 161 of Cr.P.C.
In the statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., the victim stated that around 8 months ago, the co-accused Golu had committed rape on her.
It was also stated that the applicant had made a video and on the pretext of making the video viral had committed rape on 4-5 times.
He also stated that she was pregnant and carrying a fetus of 5 months.
In the statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., it was also alleged that the co-accused Golu and four others took her to Haridwar on a trail.

4. In the light of the aforesaid, the contention of the Counsel for the applicant is that on the date in question, the applicant was visited at Khatoo Shyam Mandir at Rajasthan, which is fortified by the CDR report collected during investigation.

5. Learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the bail prayer and points out that as per the DNA report,
the fetus is that of the co-accused Golu Shukla.

Learned A.G.A. also points out that as per the radiological report, the age of the victimis 15 years, however, there is no definite documents with regard to the age of the victim in consoance with provisions of Juvenile Justice Act and the Rules framed thereunder.

6. Considering the submissions made at the bar, prima facie, the allegations levelled against Golu Shukla; although in the statement under Sections 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C., the allegations of rape was levelled against the applicant; there is no corroborating evidence in support of the said allegations and in view of the said situations coupled with the fact that the applciant has no criminal antecedents and is in custody since 04.08.2023 and there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant if enlarged on bail, would in any way adversely affect the trial and without expressing any opinion on merit, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

7. Let the applicant Alok Kumar Awasthi be released on bail in the aforesaid first information report on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
